paragraphs: Judgment center: the work of postsecondary education administrators (US O*NET-SOC 11-9033.00 Education Administrators, Postsecondary) is to turn these upstream conditions—the institution's positioning and academic standards, the needs of departments and students and faculty, teaching and research and service data, and admissions and student status and curriculum and personnel and budgets and facilities and regulations—into executable, verifiable, and accountable schooling and operating results: first set teaching and research and service goals and resource directions per the institution's positioning and academic standards and regulations, then organize curriculum and programs and staffing and academic evaluation and observe classrooms and academic affairs, then handle admissions and registration and student status and student services and faculty personnel and professional development, meanwhile prepare and execute budgets and arrange campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and safety and information systems, then liaise with education authorities and industry and international partners and write reports and assessment material, and finally adjust plans according to data and feedback and complete the handover. The key judgment is not whether you can control people, but whether you can hold the four things—goals, data, fairness, and compliance—along the chain of teaching and academic affairs, students and personnel and professional development, and budget and operations and compliance, and leave a verifiable record at every step.

Suitable to try first: willing to be responsible for the institution's teaching and research and service results and to accept questioning from students, faculty, departments, and superior authorities; able to switch rhythm among academic affairs, personnel, budgets, and logistics; willing to work within regulations, academic standards, and budget constraints and handle academic integrity and student affairs and safety matters; and able to accept meetings and longer hours driven by the academic year and semesters and admissions and assessment and supervision and budget cycles.

Choose with caution: if you expect this work to be only giving orders, or to discuss only academics without budgets and personnel, or you are unwilling to work within regulations, academic standards, and procedures, avoid academic integrity and student safety and fairness and personnel responsibility, treat disciplinary reputation as a conclusion and make major decisions on that basis, or find it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under multi-party conflict and public accountability, then the actual work experience will usually not match expectations.

Low-risk check: use the fictional departmental assessment material and anonymous course and funding data provided on this page to complete one paper exercise of writing a department or program development plan's performance goals and measures and data basis and budget and compliance verification; it only checks whether you are willing to verify item by item against goals, data, and regulations and to mark uncertainty truthfully. The exercise uses fictional material, draws no legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions, and is not equivalent to postsecondary position engagement, appointment qualification, or academic authorization.

Judgment center: whether the institution's positioning and teaching and research and service data and student and departmental needs can be turned into schooling and operating results that faculty, students, departments, and superior authorities can all take up and verify.

Work rhythm is set jointly by the academic year and semesters, admissions and assessment and supervision points, the budget cycle, and university council meetings or superior approval; there is more public accountability and many multi-party meetings, and decisions and communication need to leave a trace.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 11-9033.00 Education Administrators, Postsecondary (postsecondary education administrators). Adjacent positions—training and development managers (11-3131), education and childcare administrators, preschool and daycare (11-9031), education administrators, kindergarten through secondary (11-9032), medical and health services managers (11-9111), chief executives (11-1011) and general and operations managers (11-1021), and postsecondary teachers (25-1xxx)—have different objects and authorization; this occupation is also not the same as a postsecondary teacher. Postsecondary position engagement and appointment qualifications and academic authorization follow the jurisdiction's regulations and institutional rules, are not inferred from the position name, and must not exceed authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally.

AI can be treated as controlled data and paperwork assistance, but generated content cannot be treated as unverified curriculum or research or assessment conclusions; students and faculty and personnel and budgets and external reports and discipline remain the responsibility of named responsible persons and the institution.

Fit judgment should combine whether you can be responsible for teaching and research and service results, whether you can work with data, regulations, and budgets, whether you can communicate under multi-party conflicts of interest and escalate per the system, and whether you are clear about your authority boundaries over student data, personnel, budgets, and external reports; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of having been a teacher or being good-tempered, and all of this must be confirmed in supervised management and academic service experience.

All exercises on this page use fictional material; real curriculum, assessment, personnel, budget, compliance, safety, and discipline decisions must be undertaken by personnel with the corresponding qualifications and in accordance with the jurisdiction's regulations, institutional rules, and education administration department requirements; individuals must not exceed authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and this page does not constitute any legal, financial, or appointment advice.

The work object of this occupation is the institution and its departments with high-frequency interaction among multiple parties: the institution's positioning and academic standards and regulations; the needs of students, faculty, and departments; curriculum and teaching and research and service data; admissions and student status and program offerings; funding and budgets and procurement and assets; campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and safety and information systems; and assessment and supervision and reporting and approval arrangements. The output is schooling and operating results that meet the institution's positioning and academic standards and compliance requirements: curriculum and teaching delivered per programs and courses and training objectives, department and program development plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and personnel records completed per the system, funding and procurement and logistics and facility records executed per budget, and verifiable assessment and compliance and external reporting records. The basis for judgment is the institution's positioning, regulations, data, and institutional rules, not personal preference or the position name.

Judgment one: whether the institution's positioning and academic standards are aligned—whether programs and courses and performance goals are determined per the institution's positioning and regulations and assessment data, rather than making demands from impressions.

Judgment two: whether teaching and academic observation and course assessment are evidence-based—whether improvements are proposed per classroom observation and academic evaluation and course and material assessment and compliance requirements, rather than judging teachers by personal experience.

Judgment three: whether personnel and academic affairs communication follow the system—whether faculty and staff are recruited, trained, and evaluated per procedure and academic integrity and student affairs are handled per the system with a trace, rather than by ad hoc decisions.
Judgment four: whether budgets and procurement are held—whether preparation and execution and authorization follow the budget, funding, and procurement system, rather than using funds at will.

Judgment five: whether campuses and safety and facilities are held—whether arrangements and inspections follow the requirements for campuses, facilities, laboratories, dormitories, safety, and maintenance, rather than remedying things afterward.

Judgment six: whether data, compliance, external reporting, and discipline stay within boundaries—whether data use follows regulations, data permissions, privacy, and student and research record requirements, without exceeding authority to issue legal, financial, or personnel discipline conclusions externally, and with consultation and reporting per the system on anomalies.

Environment and rhythm: mainly institution and department offices, meetings, classrooms, and laboratory observation with high-frequency communication with students, faculty, and departments; the rhythm is driven by the academic year and semesters and admissions and assessment and supervision points and the budget cycle, with more public accountability and multi-party meetings, and decisions and communication need a trace; the specific arrangements and working hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

The work of postsecondary education administrators can be divided into three connected but independent work faces. The first is teaching and academic affairs leadership: observe teaching methods and review courses and materials to assess and unify curriculum and training objectives, work with teachers to set and maintain program and course and training standards and academic norms, determine program and course offerings and scheduling and staffing and teaching facility needs, assess course and program and project effectiveness and efficiency and compliance, organize faculty development and academic evaluation, prepare department and program development plans based on teaching and student and research data, and approve new programs or courses or propose modifications for academic committee or university council approval. The second is students and personnel and professional development: provide students with academic and scholarly and development and pathway guidance, communicate education policy and academic integrity and student affairs issues with faculty and departments and students, enforce student status and academic norms and examination and graduation review rules, recruit, train, and evaluate faculty and staff and make personnel and appointment recommendations, guide and support counselors and student affairs and special support activities, and coordinate student clubs and academic and cultural activities. The third is budget, operations, and compliance: prepare and submit budgets and resource requests and determine fund and asset allocation and authorize procurement, arrange campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and cafeterias and safety and information systems, interpret government and education authority regulations and develop compliance and academic integrity and research funding and data security plans accordingly, liaise with education authorities and industry and domestic and international institutions and track policy, develop school-enterprise and industry-research cooperation projects, write admissions and publicity and assessment and reporting material, and supervise student services and campus safety. All three work faces proceed within the institution's positioning, regulations, data, and institutional rules.
Teaching and academic affairs leadership

Determine program and course and training objectives per the institution's positioning and regulations and assessment data → observe classrooms and assess courses and materials and programs → organize faculty development and academic evaluation → prepare department and program development plans based on teaching and student and research data → approve or submit new programs and courses and modification proposals

Students and personnel and professional development

When comparing, verify item by item against the service object, authorization, compliance basis, and output, and do not swap by institution or job title, nor read management duties as legal judgment authority, financial decision authority, or personnel discipline authority.
Core purpose

Turn the institution's positioning and student and faculty and departmental needs into executable, verifiable, and accountable higher education schooling and operating results: clear program and training objectives, evidence-based data and compliance, personnel and academic affairs per the system, budgets and logistics held, and reports and discipline within boundaries.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: postsecondary teachers focus on teaching and research and academic service itself; training and development managers improve corporate employee ability and performance; preschool and daycare administrators ensure the operation of preschool and daycare institutions; primary and secondary education administrators ensure primary and secondary schooling and teaching; medical and health services managers ensure medical institution operations; chief executives set and execute overall institutional strategy and operations.
Main object and basis

The object is the institution's positioning and academic standards and regulations; students, faculty, and departments; curriculum and teaching and research and service data; admissions and student status and program offerings; funding and budgets and procurement and assets; campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and safety; and assessment and supervision and reporting and approval arrangements; the basis is the institution's positioning, regulations, data, and institutional rules.

Objects and bases of adjacent positions: courses and research itself (academic norms and institutional rules); corporate employees and training needs (corporate training and human resources systems); preschool and daycare institutions and children (preschool education and daycare regulations); primary and secondary schools and teachers and students (compulsory education and teacher regulations and district rules); patients and medical services (medical and health regulations); and the institution and investors (company law and corporate governance).
Core process

Teaching and academic affairs leadership → students and personnel and professional development → budget and operations and compliance and reporting (including faculty development, department planning, and inspection).

Processes of adjacent positions: teaching—research—academic service (postsecondary teachers); training needs analysis—curriculum development—implementation and evaluation (training and development managers); enrollment and childcare—staffing and safety—parent communication and compliance (preschool and daycare); instructional leadership—personnel and home-school relations—budget and operations (primary and secondary administrators); medical services—quality and safety—operations (medical managers); and strategy—operations—governance and disclosure (chief executives).
Main output

Curriculum and teaching delivered per programs and courses and training objectives, department and program development plans formed from data, recruitment and training and evaluation and personnel records completed per the system, funding and procurement and logistics and facility records executed per budget, and verifiable assessment and compliance and external reporting records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: courses and papers and projects (postsecondary teachers); corporate training plans and effectiveness evaluations; institutional operation and childcare and safety and compliance records; primary and secondary schooling and teaching and compliance records; medical services and quality and safety records; and strategy and operations and governance and disclosure records.
Responsible party

This occupation is responsible for organizing teaching, personnel, budgets, and logistics per the institution's positioning, regulations, and data and for student data and reports and compliance; the university council, academic committee, and superior education authority bear management responsibility for policy and budget approval and personnel discipline and compliance conclusions per regulations and systems.
Responsibilities of adjacent positions: borne by each institution's responsible persons and professionals per their own regulations and systems, with different authorization bases.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with faculty, departments, students, counselors, the superior education authority, the university council, the academic committee, and logistics, safety, information, psychology, and employment staff, and adjust priorities per the academic year and semesters and assessment and supervision and budget points; student safety, data, personnel, budget, and out-of-authority matters are consulted and reported per the system.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: with departments and research teams (postsecondary teachers); with human resources and corporate departments (training); with parents, health, and community (preschool and daycare); with teachers, parents, and supervisors (primary and secondary); with medical staff, patients, and regulators (medical); and with the board and investors (chief executives).
Conclusion boundaries

Must determine program and training objectives per the institution's positioning and regulations and data; must observe classrooms and assess courses per the system; must recruit and evaluate and make personnel appointment recommendations per procedure; must prepare and execute per the budget and procurement system; must arrange and inspect per the requirements for campuses, facilities, laboratories, dormitories, and safety; must use student and research and personnel data per data permissions and privacy; and must not exceed authority to issue legal or financial or personnel discipline conclusions externally.
The boundaries of adjacent positions are determined by their own object, regulations, and institutional rules; similar institution or job titles do not mean duties can be interchanged.
In this work, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four categories: first, the institution's positioning is disconnected from programs and training objectives, making teaching and assessment requirements inconsistent and planning unfounded; second, teaching and programs are assessed by impression rather than data and observation, distorting decisions and causing teacher attrition; third, personnel and academic affairs and budgets and procurement are handled without the system, procedures, and budget constraints, creating compliance, fairness, and interpersonal risks; fourth, student and research data and reports and discipline go out of bounds or campuses and safety and facilities are not held, creating privacy, safety, and accountability risks. The verification method is that each item has a reviewable basis: program and training objectives and department development plans, classroom observation and academic evaluation and course assessment and compliance records, recruitment and training and evaluation and personnel and appointment recommendation records, budget and procurement and logistics and facility and safety records, and student and research data and reports and discipline and compliance records, rather than memory or verbal understanding.

Are recruitment, training, evaluation, personnel and appointment recommendations, and academic integrity and student status handling done per procedure with a trace, rather than by ad hoc decisions?
Are budgets, funding, procurement, and allocation prepared and executed and authorized per the system, rather than used at will?

When a student safety incident, data leak, research funding or procurement anomaly, academic integrity or discipline overreach, or out-of-authority external report occurs, is it handled in the order of first protecting student and personnel safety and preserving evidence, stopping the affected link, recording and reporting per the process, and involving the superior education authority and legal affairs and academic committee when necessary?

Mainly institution and department offices, meetings, classrooms, and laboratory observation with high-frequency communication with students, faculty, and departments; the rhythm is driven by the academic year and semesters and admissions and assessment and supervision points and the budget cycle, with more public accountability and multi-party meetings, and decisions and communication need a trace; the specific arrangements and working hours follow the institution and jurisdiction.

Quality looks at whether the institution's positioning and program and training objectives are aligned, whether classroom observation and academic observation and assessment are evidence-based, whether personnel and academic affairs and budgets follow the system, whether campuses and safety and facilities are held, and whether student and research data and reports and compliance are verifiable.

This page corresponds to US O*NET 11-9033.00: planning, directing, or coordinating student teaching, administrative, and service activities and research and educational activities at a higher education institution. The main work faces include academic affairs, admissions and student status and student services, personnel coordination, and budgets and institutional operations; the specific division of labor follows the position authorization, and it cannot be assumed that every administrator has all functions. This table compares postsecondary education administrators row by row with six adjacent positions that are easily confused by institutional name and education management duties, or that have rotation and transfer relationships, on core work and output, key differences, and selection basis. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them, but to explain their respective service objects, authorization, and compliance boundaries—especially that legal judgment authority, financial decision authority, and personnel discipline authority cannot all be borne by this occupation.

When comparing, rely on three things: first, the work object (corporate employees and training needs, preschool and daycare institutions and children, primary and secondary schools and their teachers and students, patients and medical services, courses and research itself, and overall institutional strategy and operations); second, the basis and authorization (the institution's positioning, regulations, data, and institutional rules; corporate training and human resources systems; preschool education and daycare regulations; compulsory education and teacher regulations and district rules; medical and health regulations; academic norms and institutional rules; and company law and corporate governance each apply separately); third, the output and responsibility (who is responsible for higher education schooling and operations, who for corporate training, who for preschool and daycare institutions, who for primary and secondary schooling, who for medical services, who for courses and research itself, and who for overall institutional strategy). Where the three are inconsistent, the position's actual duties and the regulations and institutional rules prevail.

The selection basis can follow three clues: if you want to carry teaching and academic affairs and schooling and operations and compliance responsibility in a higher education institution, this page's occupation is the closest; if you want to do training and development in a company, or work in preschool and daycare institutions, primary and secondary schools, medical institutions, postsecondary teaching and research, or institutional strategy, then training and development managers, education and childcare administrators for preschool and daycare, education administrators for kindergarten through secondary, medical and health services managers, postsecondary teachers, and chief executives are adjacent paths. What must be added when transferring is the object, regulations, and authorization, not only management experience.

paragraphs: Training and Development Managers (11-3131.00)
Analyze corporate training needs and develop and implement training programs to improve employee ability and performance, responsible for training effectiveness evaluation and budgets.

The service object and basis differ: training and development managers serve corporate employees and business goals, based on corporate training and human resources systems; this page's occupation serves students, faculty, and departments in higher education institutions, based on the institution's positioning and higher education regulations and institutional rules. Observation signal one: willing to be responsible for others' teaching and research and service results and to accept questioning from students, faculty, departments, and superior authorities, and able to work with the institution's positioning and regulations and data rather than by feel.

Observation signal two: willing to work within student and research data and personnel and budget and procurement and safety and compliance systems, and confirming before acting when student academic discipline and personnel and budgets and external reporting are involved.

Observation signal three: able to keep attention to goals, data, and procedure under multi-party meetings, departmental communication, and assessment and supervision and budget cycles, and not skipping verification to save time.

Observation signal four: able to accept meetings and longer hours driven by the academic year and semesters and admissions and assessment and supervision and budget cycles, and willing to do records, reports, compliance, and handover.

Trainable abilities include program and course and training objective design, classroom observation and academic evaluation and course assessment, faculty development and department planning, recruitment and training and evaluation, departmental communication and student guidance, budget and procurement and logistics and safety and compliance management, and data and privacy and records.

Reverse signals include expecting only to give orders or to discuss only academics without budgets and personnel, being unwilling to work within regulations and academic standards and procedures, avoiding student safety and fairness and academic integrity and personnel responsibility, treating disciplinary reputation as a conclusion and making major decisions on that basis, or finding it hard to keep patience and professional boundaries under multi-party conflict and public accountability.

description.text: Postsecondary education administrators (O*NET-SOC 11-9033.00) carry schooling and operations and academic affairs management in a higher education institution: determine program and course and training objectives and department development directions per the institution's positioning and regulations and data, observe classrooms and assess courses and materials, organize faculty development and academic evaluation, handle student academics and academic integrity and student status and departmental communication, recruit, train, and evaluate faculty and staff per procedure and make personnel and appointment recommendations, prepare and execute budgets and procurement, arrange campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and safety and information systems, and interpret regulations and liaise with education authorities and industry and domestic and international institutions and write reports. US basis: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 104,590 US dollars per year (50.29 US dollars per hour, only the median provided); about 226,600 employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of Slower than average (1% to 2%), and about 15,100 projected openings; preparation level Job Zone Five, interest code SEC. Mainland China: higher education position engagement and appointment qualification and assessment and training follow the Higher Education Law, the Regulations on the Personnel Administration of Public Institutions, and education administration department and institutional provisions; public statistics have no occupation-level wage basis established, and this page visibly marks the gap where relevant.

subject.name: Postsecondary education administrators
subject.summary: Postsecondary education administrators (US O*NET-SOC 11-9033.00, Education Administrators, Postsecondary) are the schooling and operations and academic affairs management positions in higher education institutions: planning, directing, or coordinating student teaching, administrative, and service activities and research and educational activities at a higher education institution; the work includes determining program and course and training objectives and department and program development directions per the institution's positioning and academic standards and regulations, observing classrooms and reviewing courses and materials to assess and unify curriculum and instruction, working with teachers to set program and course and training standards and academic norms, determining program and course offerings and scheduling and staffing and teaching facility needs, organizing faculty development and academic evaluation, providing students with academic and scholarly and development guidance and enforcing student status and academic norms and examination and graduation review rules, communicating with teachers and departments and students, recruiting, training, and evaluating faculty and staff and making personnel and appointment recommendations, preparing and submitting budgets and resource requests and authorizing procurement, arranging campuses and facilities and laboratories and dormitories and safety and information systems, interpreting government and education authority regulations and developing compliance plans, liaising with education authorities and industry and domestic and international institutions and writing reports, and supervising student services and campus safety. US basis: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 104,590 US dollars per year (50.29 US dollars per hour; that source provides only the median and does not provide the 10/25/75/90 percentiles); the O*NET summary page gives about 226,600 employed in 2024, a 2024—2034 projection of Slower than average (Slower than average, 1% to 2%), and about 15,100 projected openings for 2024—2034 (projection-period total basis); the preparation level is Job Zone Five (SVP 8.0 and above), the education feedback is 48% master's degree and 37% doctoral degree and 8% bachelor's degree, the interest code is SEC, and there are 27 tasks. Mainland China basis: higher education position engagement and appointment qualification and assessment and training follow the Higher Education Law and the Regulations on the Personnel Administration of Public Institutions of the People's Republic of China and the relevant provisions of the education administration department and the institution, and doing teaching work in a teaching position requires obtaining the higher education teacher qualification per the Teachers Law and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications of the People's Republic of China. Public statistics have no occupation-level wage basis corresponding to this occupation established, and this page truthfully keeps the gap, with the industry average wage serving only as a visible industry proxy.
